content.text: A yoga mat is a personal tool — the right one depends entirely on your practice style, body, and priorities. We tested 10 mats across five categories to give you honest, practical guidance.
What to Look for in a Yoga Mat

items: Grip: Critical for Vinyasa and hot yoga — look for natural rubber or PER material
Thickness: 4–6mm for cushioning, 1–3mm for balance sensitivity (Pilates/Yin)
Material: Natural rubber > PVC for eco-friendliness and grip
Length: Standard 68-72 inches; tall practitioners need 80+ inches
Stickiness vs. texture: Sticky for grip, textured for dry hands feel

content.text: After extensive testing, the Manduka PRO remains the gold standard. The closed-cell surface prevents sweat absorption and bacterial growth, the 6mm density protects joints in standing poses, and the lifetime guarantee makes it a true one-time investment.

items.question: How thick should a yoga mat be?
items.answer: 4–6mm is standard for most yoga styles and provides a good balance of cushioning and stability. 3mm is better for balance-intensive practices or travel. Anything over 6mm can feel too unstable for standing poses.

items.question: How do I clean a yoga mat?
items.answer: Spray with a 1:20 mixture of tea tree oil and water, or a commercial mat cleaner. Wipe down after every use. Deep clean monthly by hand-washing with mild soap and cold water. Never put a yoga mat in the dryer.
